name: Sticker-Style Explainer Animation. Category: Motion Design and Cinematography. Provenance is supplemental, and the name is a descriptive combination of sticker graphics and educational explanation, not an established art movement.
visualIdentity: Explicit: scientific objects and symbols become consistent stickers with white borders, rounded silhouettes, and light shadows. Concepts keep stable colors or symbols. Sequences follow a question, objects, mechanism, and conclusion, using short labels and purposeful arrows. Decoration must never obscure the explanation.
suitableUses: Explicit: concept walkthroughs and explanatory sequences, delivered as video or interactive HTML. Explicit combinations cite science communication, health or climate explainers with key figures, and classroom lessons. Inferred: social-media science explainers, since the style is built for short sequences.
limitations: Stickers must not obscure chart axes, values, or essential copy. Chart marks stay flat without white sticker borders, and bouncing chart marks are avoided. Handwritten notes must not replace primary labels. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over video, textures, outlines, or animated lighting. Gradients are disabled. Style-level exceptions are unspecified beyond these.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F5EFDF for layout; foreground #2C424D for text and lines; accent_1 #FFFFFF reserved for sticker borders; accent_2 #73A59E and accent_3 #D28C67 for concept colors. Task-supplied exact colors override these. Body text should use foreground on background (9.177:1) or accent_1 on foreground (10.534:1). accent_2 and accent_3 are decorative only, below 4.5:1 against foreground. Only notation is normalized; colors must not be darkened or recolored automatically.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit motion vocabulary: placing, peeling, path movement, and restrained bounce. Production guidance forbids automatically adding springs, bounce, or floating, so bounce must be an authored choice. Video state derives from seekable composition time, while hover, scroll, and pointer input belong only to interactive delivery. Deliberate cuts and reading holds are preserved. Interactive HTML may use a step-based stepper with an accessible transcript or table.
audio: Unspecified in the style. No music, voiceover, or effects are assigned. The audio direction is a suggestion process: choose background music, voiceover, vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence based on topic, audience, and cadence. No genre, tempo, or voice is mandatory. Speech intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture synchronization must be verified.
assetRequirements: Required: stickers of scientific objects and symbols with white borders, rounded silhouettes, and light shadows. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Approved source artwork and exact copy must be preserved unchanged. Optional sources include SVG drawing, tldraw exports, Rough.js sketch interiors, and authorized map tiles if Leaflet is used. Specific file formats and sizes are unspecified.
combinations: Explicit optional pairings, neither mandatory. style-097 adds accurate D3/SVG charts that stickers point to, with flat unbordered marks. style-024 adds handwritten arrows and short notes linking mechanism steps, using the foreground token. Motion references motion-012 and motion-015 are optional; choose none unless the scene's actions genuinely support them.
productionApproach: Style renderer: SVG is the core technology, with PixiJS, D3, tldraw, Rough.js, Cytoscape.js, or Leaflet optional for specific needs. Motion engine: Motion, mo.js, or Anime.js optional, with one owner per animated property. Render pipeline: HyperFrames is primary. Remotion is fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation applies, and the reason must be recorded. Pipeline handles assembly, sync, validation, and export. Verify seeks, decoded frames, palette, and audio before delivery.
